title: Serving UC trace location must read MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID directly, not through _get_experiment_id
answers: UC-bound experiment traces go to inference table instead of Unity Catalog tables in Databricks Model Serving
Model serving traces not landing in UC experiment tables
Why does _resolve_experiment_uc_location fall back in serving
Experiment does not exist error when resolving UC trace location in serving
body:
Symptom: In Databricks Model Serving, traces for a Unity Catalog-bound experiment are routed to the inference-table path instead of the UC-backed experiment tables.
Root cause: mlflow/tracing/provider.py:_resolve_experiment_uc_location called _get_experiment_id(), which validates the id against the local tracking store. The experiment does not exist there in a serving container, so it raised and UC resolution never succeeded.
Fix pattern: when in_serving, take the id from MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID.get(); use _get_experiment_id() only outside serving. Keep the existing early return when the id is empty.
Constraints: applies only to the serving branch. Non-serving tracing still validates through _get_experiment_id(). The serving path then looks the experiment up in the Databricks store (_get_store('databricks')).
applies: Serving-only branch of UC trace location resolution in mlflow/tracing/provider.py.
says: Model serving traces are landing in inference tables instead of Unity Catalog experiment tables.
Deployments throw an experiment does not exist error when routing traces in model serving.
Model endpoint traces should appear in the catalog experiment rather than inference storage.
Traces collected from served model endpoints fail to route to Unity Catalog destination tables.
Unity Catalog experiment destination is ignored and serving traces fall back to inference tables.
search: In Databricks Model Serving, _resolve_experiment_uc_location in mlflow/tracing/provider.py must retrieve the experiment id directly from MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID.get() rather than calling _get_experiment_id(). Calling _get_experiment_id() in serving containers raises an error because the experiment does not exist in local tracking storage, preventing resolution and erroneously routing Unity Catalog traces to inference tables. Outside serving, _resolve_experiment_uc_location continues validating via _get_experiment_id(), while the serving path resolves the experiment through _get_store('databricks').
